content:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel tweak we saw p99 regress ~120ms for streaming chat on g4dn pools when mb_size >= 8. Not steady; tail spikes on multi-turn sessions.
aj: Ack. Do we have an experiment id or job link?
sam: Putting logs here: `s3://redwood-perf/2026-03/streaming-regress/exp-042.log` — shows long tail in send_chunk time, KV cache hit rate drops around spike windows.
luis: KV cache drop would explain extra recompute? Which kernel was selected in those windows?
maria: The runtime switched from fused-attn-v2 -> fallback-matmul for some requests (see profiler traces). I think the kernel selector is flipping because sequence lengths vary when clients stream delta tokens.
aj: Can you paste the profiler snippet?
maria: ```
# profiler excerpt
timestamp: 2026-03-16T22:11:02Z
model: gpt-lite-7b
kernel: fallback-matmul
seq_len: 512 -> 768
mb_size: 8
kv_cache_hits: 72%
send_chunk_ms_p99: 310
```
sam: That kernel flip is suspicious — fallback path has worse per-token latency at short tail. We need to verify kernel scoring: maybe it uses avg seq len rather than percentile.
elain: (I think you meant elaine) quick note: streaming's chunking causes intermittent longer sequences when client sends context/edits; distribution isn't stationary. Kernel selector should be robust to p99 seq length, not mean.
maria: Exactly — current policy uses mean_seq_len_est over 30s window. If a few long sessions start, they change batch shape and flip kernel choice for the whole microbatch. Bad.
aj: Two quick hypotheses: 1) selector uses mean -> flip and regresses, 2) mb_size 8 increases probability of mixing short+long requests in same microbatch and amplifies tail.
luis: Can we repro locally with synthetic traffic? I can send a mix: 80% short chat (64 tokens), 20% long continuation (700 tokens), mb_size sweep 1,2,4,8.
sam: Yep please run. Also capture kernel decisions with `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel;KVS_DEBUG=1`.
luis: Ran it. Quick summary: mb_size 1/2 p99 ~ 120ms; mb_size 4 ~ 160ms; mb_size 8 ~ 310ms. Kernel changed to fallback-matmul at mb>=4 when long requests present. KV hit drops by ~18% at mb=8.
maria: Interesting — KV hit drop suggests cross-batch eviction or warming delays. Do we have KV cache size/eviction policy logs?
sam: We log per-shard cache occupancy. For mb=8 runs we see short spikes of cache-evict events coincident with kernel flips. Possibly because bigger microbatches increase peak memory pressure so runtime evicts active KV shards pre-emptively.
aj: That can cause recompute of keys -> added latency. Two levers: limit mb_size for streaming pools, or change kernel selector to consider p95 seq len and not flip on brief mean change.
elaine: Also consider prioritizing streaming responses to use a conservative kernel (fused-attn-v1) that favors latency over throughput when `is_streaming=true`.
maria: Good idea. We can implement a per-request kernel bias: if request.streaming then prefer low-tail kernel.
luis: Quick patch test: add `kernel_bias=low_tail` for streaming requests. Re-ran sweep: mb8 p99 dropped from 310 -> 170ms, KV hit stable. Throughput took a ~6% hit but tail improved.
sam: Can you post the two microbench outputs?
luis: ```
# before bias
mb=8 p50: 40ms p95: 120ms p99: 310ms throughput: 320 req/s
# after bias
mb=8 p50: 45ms p95: 95ms p99: 170ms throughput: 300 req/s
```
aj: That looks like a reasonable tradeoff for interactive streaming. For non-streaming completions we should keep current selector to maximize throughput.
maria: Agreed. We need rollout plan: 1) default kernel_bias=low_tail for streaming pools, 2) expose override on route config, 3) metrics + alert for throughput drop >15% or cost uptick.
sam: Also add a quick fix to selector to use p95_seq_len over 30s window rather than mean. That reduces flip frequency.
luis: One more weirdness: when we bias kernel but keep mb_size high, we still occasionally see tiny spikes — investigate scheduling hot spots (cpu/gpu co-location). I captured perf counters showing context-switches during spikes.
maria: OK add infra ticket to look at GPU scheduling and memory fragmentation. For now let's implement kernel bias + p95 selector.
aj: PRs?
maria: I'll open one for the selector change. Sam please add the route config flag. Luis can you add the perf job to CI?
sam: On it, PR link will be in thread when ready.
luis: I'll add the CI microbench that reproduces the mixed short/long pattern.
maria: Thanks all. Quick summary for oncall: if you see p99 streaming >250ms trigger channel eng-runtime and tag me.
infra-bot: Incident rule created: alert(name="streaming_tail_p99", threshold=250ms, channel="#eng-runtime", owner="maria")
aj: Nice. Follow-up: we should document best-practice mb_size for streaming vs completions in the runtime docs. I'll draft a short blurb. :memo:
maria: Perfect. Closing loop after PRs land and we run canary on a small fraction of streaming traffic. :thumbsup:
